I am thinking about my land this year. I have 7 mu, and I always plant wheat in winter and maize in summer. That is what we do here in Quzhou. My father did it, my neighbors do it, I do it.

Last year wheat gave me about 450 kg per mu, maize about 550 kg per mu. Not bad. I will do mostly the same this year because changing too much is dangerous. Six mouths to feed.

For wheat: I buy the improved seed from the dealer in town — everyone around me uses it now, the old seed gives less. I put two bags of compound fertilizer (NPK) before planting, that is about 50 kg per mu, plus I top-dress with urea in spring when the wheat wakes up, maybe 15 kg per mu of urea. So nitrogen comes to around 18-20 kg per mu total. Phosphorus maybe 8 kg, potassium 6 kg — the compound fertilizer has all three. I irrigate from my well — winter water once before freeze, then spring water at jointing, and once more at grain filling. Three times. Pesticide twice — once for aphids, once for the rust if I see it. I plough the field after maize harvest, that is how we do it.

For maize: I plant hybrid seed, no question, everyone does. After wheat harvest I do no-tillage planting — saves time because I need to get the maize in fast. Fertilizer — I put compound at planting and urea at big trumpet stage. Nitrogen around 22 kg per mu, maize eats a lot of nitrogen. Phosphorus 6 kg, potassium 5 kg. Irrigate twice from the well if the rain is not enough. Pesticide once or twice for the borer.

I would rather put a little extra fertilizer than lose yield. Fertilizer costs money but a bad harvest is worse.
